title: By the Blood of the Lamb
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: We conquer by the blood of the Lamb and the word of our testimony. If you're stuck in a ditch this morning, remember: you have already died with Christ.
exhortation: How do we conquer? By the blood of the Lamb: by putting our faith in the finished work of Christ. And by remembering our testimony of God's grace in our lives. We speak to our own hearts and say, "Yes, it's true, I'm weak, but I am in Christ and he is strong." And when Satan accuses, we say, "You're right that I'm a sinner, but you're wrong that it's too late to repent. Jesus came not for the healthy but for the sick. He came for me, and I am his." Satan has no power and no answer to the blood of Jesus.

And what does it mean that "they loved not their lives even unto death"? It means exactly what you think. We need to be ready to die for our faith, and to live boldly and even dangerously for the name of Jesus. We are in a war. We shouldn't be surprised when the enemy shoots at us.

One of my favorite shows, Band of Brothers, illustrates this. A terrified soldier admits to his lieutenant that when he should have been helping his fellow soldiers, he hid in a ditch. The lieutenant tells him, in effect, that everyone is scared, but he hid because he still thought there was hope of getting out alive. The only way to function as a soldier is to accept that you are already dead.

Hope is only good if you're hoping in something good, dependable and sure. If you find yourself stuck in a ditch this morning, it might help to remember that you are already dead: "I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me." Stop putting your hope in dead and dying things. Put your hope in Christ, who conquered death and lives forever.

No one makes it out alive anyway. Death could come tomorrow in a car accident or at 96 in a nursing home, but it will come, and in that moment you want a good answer to the question, "What did I live for?" Do you want to look back on a life well lived? Then start dying. Die to yourself, to sin, to money, to food, to alcohol, to drugs, to fame, to laziness. And when people ask how you changed, say, "I didn't. I couldn't. I'm dead. It was Christ in me who did it."
prayer: Lord, what a glorious day it was when you rescued us. Fill us with courage today to put to death everything that is hindering us. Satan would love for us to stay huddled in that ditch and never come out. Help us see you risen and glorified, and remember the day you snatched us out of the grave when we were completely hellbound.

Help us get out of the ditch. Where there are clear areas of conviction, where we know we aren't living as we should, let them be put to death today, so that unhindered we may worship you fully, speak of you boldly and live for you completely. Jesus, how we need you.
